newsitem.title: USA: G3 to allow further dlr rise - German bank economist.
newsitem.headline: G3 to allow further dlr rise - German bank economist.

text.p: The United States, Japan and Germany are unlikely to take any action to rein in the dollar unless it shoots over 130 yen and 1.80 marks, Deutsche Bank chief economist Norbert Walter said on Friday.
"Anything up to 1.80 marks and 130 yen doesn't make (them) nervous," he told reporters here. The dollar is currently trading at 126 yen and around 1.7250 marks.

Walter said the dollar would be held back by a widely-held view in the currency markets that the currency cannot be strong when the U.S. current account deficit is so large -- a view he added that he does not share.

Walter put the prospects of a successful launch of European monetary union in 1999 at 65 percent. He said he believes that Ireland will join in and added that it would be very difficult to exclude Portugal and Spain.
Whether Italy is a founding member or not ultimately depends on the country itself, he added.

If Rome acts to reform its pension system and to bring its budget deficit for 1998 down close to three percent of gross domestic product, it would be very diffcult for Germany or other countries to exclude it, Walter said.
